prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: hospital automated medication dispensing/initial returns; timely fulfillment, pharmacist oversight, traceability, clinical control. No explicit modes.
Aliases: Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician.
Morrowglass accepts orders from authorized clinical systems, timestamps arrivals, checks required fields/patient identifiers/medication codes/quantities/destinations, routes pharmacy review, communicates status to authorized hospital systems, flags missing data/duplicates/active-record conflicts, and produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot documenting discrepancies.
Juniper displays queued orders/validation results, supports final verification before delivery/ward release, and preserves auditable review decisions/status changes.
Clinical Pharmacist assesses appropriateness/dose limits/allergies/interactions before approval, resolves professional-judgment questions, produces Dose Exception Review Slip for documented exceptions, and determines excursion-affected medication suitability under approved procedures.
Copperfield performs approved preparation; investigates administrative discrepancies, requests approved-channel clarification, escalates discrepancies to Clinical Pharmacist; checks packaging/identity/lot/expiry and cooler status/handling limits before use; produces Cold Chain Handoff Card documenting custody/conditions.
Cinderwake prepares only reviewed/authorized eligible orders, records handling, and produces Priority Refill Tote Tag for eligible refills.
Bluejay maintains facility-approved refrigeration; continuous sensors timestamp temperatures and report excursions/connectivity loss. Retain records establishing excursion duration/extent; segregate affected stock pending authorized pharmacy assessment/disposition.
Medication Safety Officer oversees safety, reviews discrepancy/handling trends, supports procedure updates, and produces Diversion Review Packet for documented diversion concerns.
East Tube Dispatch Console/West Tube Dispatch Console control authorized routing; Pneumatic Tube Network transports compatible deliveries between designated locations under procedures. Hospital Courier moves authorized medications/returns when automated routes unavailable/unsuitable.
Tallowmere records return details and produces Return Bin Audit Label per transaction; segregate returns from usable stock pending disposition.
Charge Nurse coordinates ward readiness/constraints/disruption escalation. Biomedical Engineer maintains equipment; IT Operations Specialist monitors connectivity/availability.
Unresolved discrepancies block preparation; dispensing requires completed checks/authorized status. Ward access requires local authorization, patient-care requirements, applicable cabinet controls.

New part:
S050: The Biomedical Engineer, known locally as Stonewake, supports technical recovery for dispensing and transport equipment.
S051: The East Tube Dispatch Console monitors capsule movement and records route, timing, and equipment status for each dispatch.
S052: The East Tube Dispatch Console sends a Tube Route Exception Ticket when a dispatch cannot follow its assigned route or complete delivery within the configured interval.
S053: Dispatch personnel hold affected capsules and prevent additional traffic from entering a route with an unresolved fault.
S054: Operations staff review queue status and coordinate any approved alternate route with the affected wards.
S055: The Pneumatic Tube Network remains unavailable on a segment until testing confirms that it is safe for service.
S056: A Pharmacy Technician verifies capsule contents and order identifiers before a delayed medication is released for another delivery attempt.
S057: The Clinical Pharmacist reviews any medication whose storage conditions or delivery timing may affect its suitability for use.
S058: The Registered Nurse confirms whether the ward still requires the medication and follows the approved contingency process if delivery is delayed.
S059: The Charge Nurse keeps ward staff informed about expected delivery delays and any approved local workaround.
S060: The Biomedical Engineer inspects tube hardware, switches, and sensors when a route fault indicates a physical problem.
S061: The IT Operations Specialist checks console connectivity, interface health, and relevant system logs when a fault may be software related.
S062: Dispatch resumes only after the affected route has passed its required checks and operations has authorized its return to use.
S063: Cabinet downtime is coordinated as a controlled service interruption so ward staff can use an approved alternative without losing medication accountability.
S064: The Charge Nurse sends a Cabinet Downtime Notice when a cabinet must be taken out of service or cannot support normal dispensing.
S065: The affected ward follows its approved contingency procedure and confirms access to an authorized dispensing location.
S066: The North Ward Cabinet Controller reports cabinet availability and prevents dispensing when its recorded state is Out of Service.
S067: The South Ward Cabinet Controller applies the same availability controls for its assigned ward.
S068: The Biomedical Engineer evaluates cabinet hardware and verifies safe operation after repair or component replacement.
S069: The IT Operations Specialist checks controller communications and application health when cabinet access or status reporting is impaired.
S070: The Charge Nurse confirms that clinical staff have been notified before normal cabinet use is restored.
S071: The responsible technical staff document the fault, corrective action, and verification results in the applicable service record.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
